environment: candidate checkout and the assembled pinned xverse-platform target; offline, Python 3.11+ with the admitted dependencies, C++20 tooling for the owned observation producer fixture and the built-and-installed wheel; bounded neutral fixtures, hostile malformed evidence and temporary output roots; no network, production or legacy runtime.
expected: Every read path is confined and bounded before I/O; the caller limits stay authoritative; structurally corrupt evidence is exported as an assessed status of incomplete with the recorded manifest facts preserved separately and never as primary complete; strict nested schemas, required identity, per-run eventId uniqueness, monotonic ingestionOrdinal, run-ID consistency and finite values emit only stable bounded diagnostics with no uncaught TypeError/ValueError; every manifest publication enforces the actual canonical serialized byte bound and preserves the prior manifest on a bound or I/O failure without claiming closure; and mutating an admitted caller object or a returned view after admission cannot lower an obligation, rewrite an indexed artifact hash or change an exported selection.
intended_use: A security-minded integrator supplies hostile evidence (a traversal/absolute/symlink/non-regular manifest, stream or artifact path, an oversized manifest or event line, a damaged manifest that echoes permissive limits, a manifest that recorded 'complete' whose stream is truncated or corrupt, malformed nested containers and unsupported versions) and a caller that mutates admitted obligations and returned views after admission, and expects every terminal-review repair AR-F01-AR-F05 (frozen adversarial cases ARGUS2-ADV-01-ARGUS2-ADV-07) to hold end to end through the public API and CLI.
title: Adversarial repair validation: confined bounded I/O, assessed corruption, strict schemas, publication byte bound and admission snapshot isolation
